title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
why_read: A technically elegant few-shot anomaly detection method using flow matching in a pretrained feature space achieves strong benchmark results with minimal normal-only training data.
analysis: Flownomaly reframes anomaly detection as recovering what a 'normal' version of a given image patch would look like, using a flow-matching model trained only on defect-free examples in a frozen DINOv2 feature space. Because the learned paths are straight, a single step can recover an estimate of the clean normal feature without needing iterative sampling, which keeps inference fast. It reports state-of-the-art accuracy on standard industrial anomaly benchmarks like MVTec-AD and VisA with as little as one example per category. This is a solid, incremental but practically relevant advance for industrial quality inspection using few-shot learning.
